he:Shabbat Eve Mincha/Song of Songs:10.en: The one sitting in the gardens, friends are listening to your voice, make me hear:

he:Shabbat Eve Mincha/Song of Songs:11.en: Master of the worlds, may it be Your will...

he:Shabbat Eve Mincha/Song of Songs:12.en: One who did not have time to say the entire Song of Songs before accepting Shabbat, should say these four verses whose acronym is Ya'akov:

parts.text: רִבּוֹן עָלְמִין דְּאַנְתְּ הוּא חַד וְלֹא בְחֻשְבָּן,
אַנְתְּ הוּא עִלָּאָה עַל כָּל עִלָּאִין,
לְאַנְהָגָא בְּהוֹן עָלְמִין סְתִימִין דְּלָא אִתְגַּלְיָן,
כָּל מַאן דְּאַפְרִישׁ חַד מִן חַבְרֵיהּ מֵאִלֵּין עֲשַׂר סְפִירָן אִתְחַשִׁיב לֵיהּ כְּאִלּוּ אַפְרִישׁ בָּךְ: וְאִלֵּין עָשָׂר סְפִירָן אִינוּן אַזְלִין כְּסִדְרָן,
לֹא לְעֵילָּא וְלֹא לְתַתָּא וְלֹא מִכָּל סִטְרָא,
דְּאִתְקְרִיאוּ גּוּפָא לְגַבֵּי לְבוּשִׁין דִּמְכַסִין עֲלֵיהוֹן,
יְסוֹד סִיּוּמָא דְּגוּפָא אוֹת בְּרִית קֹדֶשׁ,
מַלְכוּת פֶּה תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה קָרֵינָן לָהּ: חָכְמָה מוֹחָא אִיהִי מַחְשָׁבָה מִלְּגָאו,
וְעַל אִלֵּין תְּרֵין כְּתִיב הַנִּסְתָּרוֹת לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ,
</small> מִלְּגָאו אִיהוּ יו"ד ק"א וָא"ו ק"א,
פִּטּוּם הַקְּטֹרֶת כֵּיצַד: שְׁלשׁ מֵאוֹת וְשִׁשִּׁים וּשְׁמוֹנָה מָנִים הָיוּ בָהּ. שְׁלשׁ מֵאוֹת וְשִׁשִּׁים וַחֲמִשָּׁה כְּמִנְיַן יְמוֹת הַחַמָּה,
שֶׁמֵּהֶם מַכְנִיס כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל מְלֹא חָפְנָיו בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים,
וְשׁוֹחֲקָן יָפָה יָפָה כְּדֵי שֶׁתְּהֵא דַקָּה מִן הַדַּקָּה. וְאַחַד עָשָׂר סַמְּמָנִין הָיוּ בָהּ. וְאֵלּוּ הֵן:
מִשְׁקַל שִׁשָּׁה עָשָׂר שִׁשָּׁה עָשָׂר מָנֶה,
יֵין קַפְרִיסִין סְאִין תְּלָתָא וְקַבִּין תְּלָתָא,
וְאִם לֹא מָצָא יֵין קַפְרִיסִין מֵבִיא חֲמַר חִוַּרְיָן עַתִּיק,
כָּל שֶׁהוּא. רַבִּי נָתָן הַבַּבְלִי אוֹמֵר: אַף כִּפַּת הַיַּרְדֵּן כָּל שֶׁהִיא,
וְאִם חִסַּר אֶחָד מִכָּל סַּמָנֶיהָ חַיָּב מִיתָה: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: הַצֳּרִי אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא שְׂרָף הַנּוֹטֵף מֵעֲצֵי הַקְּטָף. בֹּרִית כַּרְשִׁינָה לָמָה הִיא בָאָה,
כְּדֵי שֶׁתְּהֵא נָאָה. יֵין קַפְרִיסִין לָמָה הוֹא בָא כְּדֵי לִשְׁרוֹת בּוֹ אֶת הַצִּפֹּרֶן כְּדֵי שֶׁתְּהֵא עַזָּה,
אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין מַכְנִיסִין מֵי רַגְלַיִם בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ מִפְּנֵי הַכָּבוֹד:
יְהֵא שְׁמֵהּ רַבָּא מְבָרַךְ לְעָלַם וּלְעָלְמֵי עָלְמַיָּא. יִתְבָּרַךְ. וְיִשְׁתַּבַּח. וְיִתְפָּאַר. וְיִתְרוֹמַם. וְיִתְנַשֵּׂא. וְיִתְהַדָּר. וְיִתְעַלֶּה. וְיִתְהַלָּל שְׁמֵהּ דְּקֻדְשָׁא,

he:Shabbat Eve Mincha/Mincha:33.en: On Asara B'Tevet, the reading is Vayechal Moshe:

he:Shabbat Eve Mincha/Mincha:34.en: Reading and Haftarah for Asara B'Tevet

he:Shabbat Eve Mincha/Amidah:2.en: For we shall call upon the name of the Lord; give greatness to our God:

parts.en: During the Ten Days of Repentance:
Who causes the dew to fall.
Who causes the wind to blow and the rain to fall.
During the Ten Days of Repentance:

he:Shabbat Eve Mincha/Amidah:13.en: In the Chazzan's repetition, we say Kedushah:

he:Shabbat Eve Mincha/Amidah:14.en: We sanctify You and glorify You as the pleasant conversation of the holy seraphim, who say before You: As it is written by the hand of Your prophet:

he:Shabbat Eve Mincha/Amidah:15.en: Holy, Holy, Holy is the Lord of Hosts. The whole earth is filled with His glory. And they praise and say:

he:Shabbat Eve Mincha/Amidah:16.en: Blessed is the glory of the Lord from His place. And in Your holy words it is written:

he:Shabbat Eve Mincha/Amidah:17.en: The Lord shall reign forever; Your God, O Zion, for all generations. Hallelujah.

parts.text: וּקְדוֹשִׁים בְּכָל יוֹם יְהַלְלוּךָ סֶּלָה. כִּי אֵל מֶלֶךְ גָדוֹל וְקָדוֹשׁ אָתָּה. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה,

parts.en: During the Ten Days of Repentance:

he:Shabbat Eve Mincha/Amidah:23.en: On the 10th of Tevet, the Chazzan says here Aneinu:

he:Shabbat Eve Mincha/Amidah:24.en: Answer us, O Lord, answer us on the day of our fast, for we are in great distress. Do not turn away from our iniquities, nor hide Your face from us, nor disregard our supplication. Be near to our cry for help. Let Your mercy comfort us. Before we call, answer us, as it is said: 'Before they call, I will answer; while they are still speaking, I will hear.' For You, O Lord, are the One who answers in time of distress, Redeemer and Savior in every time of distress and anguish. Blessed are You, O Lord, who answers the people Israel in time of distress.

parts.text: <small>(אֲרוּכָה וּמַרְפֵּא לְכָל תַּחֲלוּאֵינוּ וּלְכָל מַכְאוֹבֵינוּ וּלְכָל מַכּוֹתֵינוּ)</small>

הרוצה להתפלל בעד החולה יאמר כאן תחינה זו: יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶיךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהַי וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתַי. שֶׁתִּשְׁלַח מְהֵרָה רְפוּאָה שְׁלֵמָה מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם. רְפוּאַת הַנֶּפֶשׁ וּרְפוּאַת הַגּוּף לְחוֹלֶה (פב"פ)
parts.en: May it be Your will, O Lord our God and God of our fathers, that You send quickly a complete healing from heaven, healing of the soul and healing of the body, for the sick person (name and mother's name) among the other sick of Israel.

May it be Your will, O Lord our God and God of our fathers, that You send quickly a complete healing from heaven, healing of the soul and healing of the body, for the sick person (name and mother's name) among the other sick of Israel.

parts.text: בָּרֵךְ עָלֵינוּ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ אֶת הַשָּׁנָה הַזֹּאת. וְאֶת כָּל מִינֵי תְּבוּאָתָהּ לְטוֹבָה. וְתֵן

טַל וּמָטָר לִבְרָכָה עַל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה. וְשַׂבְּעֵנוּ מִטּוּבָהּ. וּבָרֵךְ שְׁנָתֵנוּ כַּשָּׁנִים הַטּוֹבוֹת לִבְרָכָה. כִּי אֵל טוֹב וּמֵטִיב אַתָּה וּמְבָרֵךְ הַשָּׁנִים. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה,
וְיוֹעֲצֵינוּ כְּבַתְּחִלָּה. וְהָסֵר מִמֶּנוּ יָגוֹן וַאֲנָחָה,
וּמְלֹךְ עָלֵינוּ מְהֵרָה אַתָּה יְהֹוָה לְבַדְּךָ,
וְצַדְּקֵנוּ בְּצֶדֶק וּבְמִשְׁפָּט. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה,

parts.en: During the Ten Days of Repentance:

parts.text: וְקַרְנוּ תָרוּם בִּישׁוּעָתֶךָ. כִּי לִישׁוּעָתְךָ קִוִּינוּ כָּל הַיּוֹם. וּמְצַפִּים

he:Shabbat Eve Mincha/Amidah:36.en: On the 10th of Tevet, we say here Aneinu before Shomea Tefillah:

he:Shabbat Eve Mincha/Amidah:37.en: Answer us, O Lord, answer us on the day of our fast, for we are in great distress. Do not turn away from our iniquities, nor hide Your face from us, nor disregard our supplication. Be near to our cry for help. Let Your mercy comfort us. Before we call, answer us, as it is said: 'Before they call, I will answer; while they are still speaking, I will hear.' For You, O Lord, are the One who answers in time of distress, Redeemer and Savior in every time of distress and anguish. Blessed are You, O Lord, who answers the people Israel in time of distress.

he:Shabbat Eve Mincha/Amidah:38.en: In the blessing of Shomea Tefillah, before concluding 'For You are the One who hears', one should confess with humility and a broken heart and say:

parts.text: אָנָּא יְהֹוָה חָטָאתִי. עָוִיתִי. וּפָשַׁעְתִּי לְפָנֶיךָ. מִיּוֹם הֱיוֹתִי עַל הָאֲדָמָה עַד הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה (ובפרט בחטא פלוני)
parts.en: I beg You, O Lord, I have sinned, I have transgressed, and I have rebelled before You, from the day I was born until this day (and especially in such-and-such a sin). I beg You, O Lord, do it for the sake of Your great name, and forgive me for my sins, transgressions, and rebellions, which I have sinned, transgressed, and rebelled before You, from my youth until this day, and fill all the names that I have blemished with Your great name.

parts.text: : אָנָּא יְהֹוָה. עֲשֵׂה לְמַעַן שִׁמְךָ הַגָּדוֹל. וּתְכַפֵּר לִי עַל חֲטָאַי וַעֲוֹנַי וּפְשָׁעַי. שֶׁחָטָאתִי. וְשֶׁעָוִיתִי. וְשֶׁפָּשַׁעְתִּי לְפָנֶיךָ. מִנְּעוּרַי עַד הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה. וּתְמַלֵּא כָּל הַשֵּׁמוֹת שֶׁפָּגַמְתִּי בְּשִׁמְךָ הַגָּדוֹל: </small></small>
parts.en: I beg You, O Lord, I have sinned, I have transgressed, and I have rebelled before You, from the day I was born until this day (and especially in such-and-such a sin). I beg You, O Lord, do it for the sake of Your great name, and forgive me for my sins, transgressions, and rebellions, which I have sinned, transgressed, and rebelled before You, from my youth until this day, and fill all the names that I have blemished with Your great name.

he:Shabbat Eve Mincha/Amidah:40.en: A prayer for sustenance to be said before 'For You are the One who hears':

he:Shabbat Eve Mincha/Amidah:41.en: You are the Lord God who nourishes, sustains and supports [everything] – 'from the horns of the ram to the eggs of lice.' Provide me with my portion of bread,' and let my nourishment be found – for me and all of the members of my household – before I need them; easily and not painfully; permissibly and not illegitimately; respectably and not shamefully, for life and peace, from the bounty of blessing and from the bounty of the highest blessing so that I may do Your will and be occupied with Your Torah and fulfill Your commandments. And do not make me require the gifts of flesh and blood. Rather, fulfill with me the verse in which it is written (Psalms 155:16), 'Open Your hand and satisfy the desire of all.' And it is written (Psalms 55:23), 'Cast your burden on the Lord and He will support you.'

he:Shabbat Eve Mincha/Amidah:42.en: A prayer against the withholding of rain in the Land of Israel:

he:Shabbat Eve Mincha/Amidah:43.en: And answer us, Creator of the world, with the measure of mercy, who chose His people Israel to reveal His greatness and the glory of His honor, who hears prayer. Give dew and rain upon the face of the earth, and satisfy the whole world with Your goodness, and fill our hands with Your blessings and the wealth of Your hand. Guard and save this year from all evil, from all kinds of destruction, and from all kinds of plagues. Make hope and a peaceful end for it. Have mercy and pity on us and on all our produce and livestock, and bless us with rains of blessing and generosity for life, satiety, and peace, like the good years. Remove from us plague, sword, and famine, wild beast, captivity, and disgrace, the evil inclination, and severe and difficult illnesses, and bad and difficult events. Decree for us good decrees from before You, and let Your mercies be revealed over Your attributes, and deal with Your children with the measure of mercy, and accept with mercy and favor our prayer.

parts.en: On Rosh Chodesh and on Erev Shabbat of Chol HaMoed, we say here 'Ya'aleh VeYavo':
On Rosh Chodesh and on Erev Shabbat of Chol HaMoed, we say here 'Ya'aleh VeYavo':

he:Shabbat Eve Mincha/Amidah:47.en: Our God and God of our fathers, may it ascend and come, reach, be seen, be accepted, be heard, be remembered, and be recalled, our remembrance and our visitation and the remembrance of our fathers, and the remembrance of the Messiah, the son of David, Your servant, and the remembrance of Jerusalem, Your holy city, and the remembrance of all Your people, the house of Israel, before You, for deliverance, for good, for grace and for mercy and for compassion, for good life and for peace, on the day of:

parts.text: בִּימֵי מַתִּתְיָהוּ בֶן יוֹחָנָן כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל חַשְׁמוֹנָאִי וּבָנָיו כְּשֶׁעָמְדָה מַלְכוּת יָוָן הָרְשָׁעָה עַל עַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל לְהַשְׁכִּיחָם תּוֹרָתֶךָ וּלְהַעֲבִירָם מֵחֻקֵּי רְצוֹנָךָ וְאַתָּה בְּרַחֲמֶיךָ הָרַבִּים עָמַדְתָּ לָהֶם בְּעֵת צָרָתָם רַבְתָּ אֶת רִיבָם דַּנְתָּ אֶת דִּינָם נָקַמְתָּ אֶת נִקְמָתָם מָסַרְתָּ גִבּוֹרִים בְּיַד חַלָּשִׁים וְרַבִּים בְּיַד מְעַטִּים וּטְמֵאִים בְּיַד טְהוֹרִים וּרְשָׁעִים בְּיַד צַדִּיקִים וְזֵדִים בְּיַד עוֹסְקֵי תוֹרָתֶךָ וּלְךָ עָשִׂיתָ שֵׁם גָּדוֹל וְקָדוֹשׁ בְּעוֹלָמָךְ וּלְעַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל עָשִׂיתָ תְּשׁוּעָה גְדוֹלָה וּפֻרְקָן כְּהַיּוֹם הַזֶּה וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּאוּ בָנֶיךָ לִדְבִיר בֵּיתֶךָ וּפִנּוּ אֶת הֵיכָלֶךָ וְטִהֲרוּ אֶת מִקְדָּשֶׁךָ וְהִדְלִיקוּ נֵרוֹת בְּחַצְרוֹת קָדְשֶׁךָ וְקָבְעוּ שְׁמוֹנַת (יָמִים אֵלּוּ בְּהַלֵּל וּבְהוֹדָאָה וְעָשִׂיתָ עִמָּהֶם נֵס וָפֶלֶא וְנוֹדֶה לְשִׁמְךָ הַגָּדוֹל סֶלָה:)
יְמֵי חֲנֻכָּה אֵלּוּ לְהוֹדוֹת וּלְהַלֵּל לְשִׁמְךָ הַגָּדוֹל:</small></small>

בִּימֵי מָרְדְּכַי וְאֶסְתֵּר בְּשׁוּשַׁן הַבִּירָה כְּשֶׁעָמַד עֲלֵיהֶם הָמָן הָרָשָׁע בִּקֵּשׁ לְהַשְׁמִיד לַהֲרוֹג וּלְאַבֵּד אֶת כָּל הַיְּהוּדִים מִנַּעַר וְעַד זָקֵן טַף וְנָשִׁים בְּיוֹם אֶחָד בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה עָשָׂר לְחֹדֶשׁ שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר הוּא חֹדֶשׁ אֲדָר וּשְׁלָלָם לָבוֹז וְאַתָּה בְּרַחֲמֶיךָ הָרַבִּים הֵפַרְתָּ אֶת עֲצָתוֹ וְקִלְקַלְתָּ אֶת מַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ וַהֲשֵׁבוֹתָ לוֹ גְמוּלוֹ בְרֹאשׁוֹ וְתָלוּ אוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בָּנָיו עַל הָעֵץ (וְעָשִׂיתָ עִמָּהֶם נִסִּים וְנִפְלָאוֹת וְנוֹדֶה לְשִׁמְךָ הַגָּדוֹל)

for His kindness endures forever. Let those redeemed by Adonoy say it,
those He redeemed from the adversary's hand. And from the lands He gathered them,
from the east and from the west,
from the north and from the south.<sup class="footnote-marker">3</sup>
The Targum paraphrases: the southern sea.
an inhabited city they did not find. Hungry,
also thirsty their soul fainted within them. Then they cried out to Adonoy in their distress;
from their anguish He rescued them. And He led them in a straight path,
that they might go to an inhabited city. Let them thank Adonoy for His kindness,
and for His wonders to the children of man. For He satisfied the longing soul,
and the hungry soul He filled with good. Those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death,
bound in affliction and iron.<sup class="footnote-marker">4</sup>
This refers to those who are shackled and chained and locked in the darkness of dungeons or prisons.
For they defied the words of the Almighty,
and the counsel of the Most High they scorned. And He humbled their heart with hard labor,
they stumbled and there was none to help. Then they cried out to Adonoy in their distress;
from their anguish He delivered them. He brought them out from darkness and from the shadow of death,
and their shackles He broke. Let them thank Adonoy for His kindness,
and for His wonders to the children of man. For He has broken the gates of bronze,
and the bars of iron He has cut asunder. They are fools— because of the way of their transgression and their iniquities,
they cause their own affliction. Their soul abhors all food,
and they drew near to the gates of death. Then they cried out to Adonoy in their distress;
from their anguish He delivered them. He sends His word and heals them,
and delivers them from their destruction. Let them thank Adonoy for His kindness,
and for His wonders to the children of man. And let them offer sacrifices of thanksgiving,
and declare His works with singing. Those who go down to the sea in ships,
that do work in mighty waters.<sup class="footnote-marker">5</sup>
Bodies of water with swift currents require increased efforts to keep the ship on course.
They saw the works of Adonoy,
and His wonders in the deep. He spoke and raised the stormwind,
and lifted up its waves. They rise to the heavens,
their soul melts away because of trouble. They reel and stagger like a drunkard,
and all their skills are swallowed up [useless]. Then they cried out to Adonoy in their distress,
from their anguish He rescued them. He turned the storm into calmness,
and their waves were stilled. They rejoiced because the waves were quieted,
and He led them to their desired border. Let them thank Adonoy for His kindness,
and for His wonders to the children of man. Let them exalt Him in an assembly of people,
the Talmud learns the Blessing of Thanksgiving (בִּרְכַת הַגוֹמֵל) must be recited in the presence of ten men who constitute a קָהָל ,
and at a sitting of elders,
From these words the Talmud learns that at least two of the ten men in the quorum, must be elders, Torah scholars.
He turns rivers into a wilderness,
and springs of water into an arid place. A fruitful land into a salt waste,
because of the wickedness of its inhabitants. He turns a wilderness into a pool of water,
and a dry land into springs of water. And He made the hungry settle there,
and they established an inhabited city. And they sowed fields and planted vineyards,
which yielded fruit for harvest. And He blessed them and they multiplied greatly,
He did not diminish. And they were reduced in numbers and brought low,
and sorrow. He pours contempt upon nobles,
and causes them to wander in the wasteland where there is no path. And He lifted up the needy from affliction,
and he established families like a flock. The upright will see it and rejoice,
and all iniquity will shut its mouth. Whoever is wise,
and they will understand the kindnesses of Adonoy....

en:Shabbat Eve Mincha/Amidah:41.en: You are the Lord God who nourishes, sustains and supports [everything] – 'from the horns of the ram to the eggs of lice.' Provide me with my portion of bread,' and let my nourishment be found – for me and all of the members of my household – before I need them; easily and not painfully; permissibly and not illegitimately; respectably and not shamefully, for life and peace, from the bounty of blessing and from the bounty of the highest blessing so that I may do Your will and be occupied with Your Torah and fulfill Your commandments. And do not make me require the gifts of flesh and blood. Rather, fulfill with me the verse in which it is written (Psalms 155:16), 'Open Your hand and satisfy the desire of all.' And it is written (Psalms 55:23), 'Cast your burden on the Lord and He will support you.'

parts.text: let us sound the shofar to the Rock of our deliverance.<sup class="footnote-marker">1</sup>
Israel will say these words in the days of the Messiah, when Jews will inspire each other to sing to Almighty God Who delivered them.—Radak
Let us greet His Presence with thanksgiving,
Expressions of thanksgiving are considered of the highest virtue, as it is said, ‘As for myself, with expressions of thanksgiving I sacrifice to you.’—Jonah 2
with hymns let us raise our voices unto Him. For a great Almighty is Adonoy and a great King over all gods.<sup class="footnote-marker">3</sup>
‘Are there any other gods?’ asks the Midrash, and answers by citing verse 5 of the next Psalm, ‘All the gods of the nations are idols.’
For in His hands are the depths<sup class="footnote-marker">4</sup>
Metsudas Dovid offers another translation: ‘In His hands are the hidden things of the earth,’ referring to things which require much study and thought in order to be understood.
and the heights of the mountains are His;
let us prostrate ourselves and bow;
our Maker. For He is our God and we are the people of His pasture,
and the flock of His hand,
It is possible for us to reach this high level and to be accepted as His flock even this very day, if we would hearken to His voice.—Dover Sholom
if you will heed His voice. Do not harden your heart as at Merivah,
as on the day of Massah<sup class="footnote-marker">6</sup>
The Jews complained and murmured at the lack of water during their wanderings in the wilderness (Exodus 17:1-17; Numbers 20:1-13).
in the desert. When your fathers tested Me,
<i class="footnote">The words from here till the end of the Psalm,
are the actual words of the Divine Presence that emanated from the throat of Moses,
שְׁכִינָה מְדַבֶּרֶת מִתּוֹךְ גְרוֹנוֹ שֶׁל משֶׁה — Eyun Tfiloh
though they had seen My work. Forty years I quarreled with that generation;
“They are a people of erring hearts,
and they did not know my ways.” Therefore I swore in My anger,
“They shall not enter My resting place.”<sup class="footnote-marker">8</sup>
The Holy Land is described as the land of rest (Deuteronomy 12:9).
Sing to Adonoy a new song<sup class="footnote-marker">9</sup>

Israel will sing a new song of praise to God in the future, when He gathers us together from our exile. This new song will be in addition to those we now sing.—Radak According to our Sages, every time a ‘new song’ is mentioned, it refers to future events. Fresh mercies and deliverance demand fresh expressions of thanksgiving and homage.
Sing to Adonoy all the [inhabitants of] earth. Sing to Adonoy,
proclaim His deliverance from day to day. Recount His glory among the nations,
His wonders among all the peoples. For Adonoy is great and most extolled;
He is awesome above all gods. For all the gods of the nations are idols,
whereas Adonoy made the heavens. Beauty and splendor are before Him,
strength and glory are in His Sanctuary. Ascribe to Adonoy—families of peoples— —ascribe to Adonoy honor and might! Ascribe to Adonoy the honor due His Name,
bring an offering and come to His courtyards. Prostrate yourselves before Adonoy in the splendor<sup class="footnote-marker">10</sup>

Etz Yosef understands this as the holy splendor of God’s Sanctuary. Tzelosa D’Avraham sees it as the splendor and mode of worship before God, as compared with secular or frivolous manifestations of beauty and splendor.
tremble before Him all (peoples of) the earth! Declare among the nations,
“Adonoy reigns!” for He established the world so that it cannot be moved,
He will judge the peoples with uprightness. The heavens will rejoice,

Simcha (rejoicing) describes one’s feeling at a new experience of happiness, whereas gila (exultation) describes the feeling one experiences over an ongoing situation of joy. Since there is nothing new on the earth (Koheleth) it is said that the earth will exult (gila) but the heavens will rejoice (simcha) because there is always something new in the heavens.—Gaon of Vilna
the sea and its fullness will roar. The field and all that is in it will jubilate,
then all the trees of the forest will sing for joy. Before Adonoy when He comes— when He comes to judge the earth;
He will judge mankind with justice,
When Adonoy is [universally accepted as] King<sup class="footnote-marker">12</sup>
Our Sages say that this will occur after the annihilation of Amalek. At that time God’s Name and His throne will be complete. See Exodus 10.
Those who live on these islands will rejoice.—Etz Yosef
will rejoice. Clouds and dense darkness surround Him;

These clouds and darkness will envelop and destroy the wicked, after which God’s justice and righteousness will be apparent. Others say that this is an allusion to the mystery of God’s ways, but that His kingdom is founded on righteousness.—Radak
righteousness and justice are the foundations of His throne. Fire will go before Him to surround<sup class="footnote-marker">15</sup>
God will surround them with fire so there will be no escape for them.—Radak
and burn His antagonists. His lightning illuminates the inhabited world,
the earth sees and trembles.<sup class="footnote-marker">16</sup>
The future revelation of God’s kingdom is described in terms similar to those of the revelation at Mount Sinai.
‘Mountains’ refers to the kings of the world—Etz Yosef
before the Master of all the earth. The heavens will declare His righteousness and all the peoples will behold His glory. Humiliated will be all who serve graven images,
before Him all gods will bow. Zion will hear and rejoice,
and the daughters [cities] of Judah will exult because of Your judgments,
are most high over all the earth;
You are greatly exalted above all gods.<sup class="footnote-marker">18</sup>
Etz Yosef understands ‘gods’ to refer to the sun, moon, stars, etc.
hate evil! He preserves the souls of His pious ones;
from the hand of the wicked,
He saves them. Light is sown<sup class="footnote-marker">19</sup>

Light is sown for the righteous in this world but the harvest of that light awaits the future world.—Radak Others say that the light may be hidden like the seed in the earth, but it is sure to spring forth.
and for the upright in heart—joy. Rejoice,
Shevet Musar says that the righteous ones will not merely rejoice in their personal salvation and deliverance but they will actually rejoice in God, Whose kingdom will be revealed and complete.
and give thanks to His holy Name.<sup class="footnote-marker">21</sup>
This Psalm, like the previous ones, refers to the future when God will render final judgment on the world and its inhabitants.
His right hand effected deliverance for Him [as did] His holy arm. Adonoy has made known<sup class="footnote-marker">23</sup>
This will be made known through His prophets.—Etz Yosef
before the eyes of the nations He has revealed His justice. He remembered His kindliness and faithfulness<sup class="footnote-marker">24</sup>
God will remember the kindness He promised to Israel, because of His faithfulness. —Etz Yosef
all the ends of the earth have seen the deliverance of our God. Raise your voice unto Adonoy all [inhabitants of] the earth! burst forth into exultation,
and play music! Play to Adonoy with a harp,
with harp and the sound of music. With trumpets and the sound of the
raise your voices before the King,
Adonoy. The sea and its fullness,
will roar with joy! [also] the world and those who dwell therein. Rivers will clap hands,
mountains will sing. Before Adonoy when He comes to judge the earth;
He will judge mankind with righteousness and peoples with uprightness.
When Adonoy is [universally accepted as] King,

Radak notes that Psalm 97 states that, ‘When Adonoy is (universally accepted as) King, the earth will exult.’ He explains that the people will tremble during the destruction of Gog of Magog, and only after his downfall will the earth rejoice.
[Before Him Who is] enthroned on Cherubim,
This is a reference to the golden Cherubim atop the Ark in which Moses placed the two tablets of the Law. See Exodus 25:18-22

God’s greatness will be revealed in Zion, for there He will bring all the nations to judgement.—Radak Others quote Rabbi Chanina who says that only when God returns His Schechina (Holy Presence) to Zion will His greatness be recognized. Etz Yosef understands the verse as follows: ‘God, Whose dwelling is in Zion, is great and exalted above all peoples.’
and is high above all the peoples. They will pay homage to Your Name,
It is holy. The might of the King is [evidenced in] His love of justice,
The translation of this verse follows Ibn Ezra.
justice and charity amid Jacob You have instituted. Exalt Adonoy,
and prostrate yourselves at His footstool,
‘Footstool’ is an allusion to the Holy Temple.
Others translate, ‘Holy is it,’ referring to the Holy Temple.
Moses and Aaron among His priests,
and Samuel among those who invoke His Name,
and He answered them. In a pillar of cloud He spoke to them<sup class="footnote-marker">31</sup>
Ibn Ezra understands this as a reference to Moses and Aaron alone, because God did not speak to Samuel from a pillar of cloud.
they preserved His testimonies and the statute which He gave them. Adonoy,
You were a forgiving God to them,
[yet] You took vengeance for their misdeeds.<sup class="footnote-marker">32</sup>

Moses and Aaron were punished for their role in the incident of the waters of Merivah and were not permitted to enter the Holy Land. Samuel who declared, ‘I am the Seer,’ was punished when he mistakenly thought to anoint David’s brother Eliav as king. (1 Samuel 9).
and prostrate yourselves at His holy mountain;
A Psalm of David. Ascribe to Adonoy— you sons of the mighty<sup class="footnote-marker">33</sup>

According to Targum, ‘sons of the mighty’ refers to the angels who are called upon to give praise to God. The Sages say that ‘the mighty’ refers to the Patriarchs who were mighty in their faith of God and steadfast in carrying out His will. Thus ‘sons of the mighty’ refers to all Jewry.
— ascribe to Adonoy glory and might. Ascribe to Adonoy the glory due His Name,
prostrate yourselves before Adonoy in the splendor of holiness.<sup class="footnote-marker">34</sup>
Etz Yosef says that this refers to the Bais haMikdash.
Adonoy's voice is upon the waters.<sup class="footnote-marker">35</sup>
God’s voice was heard when He split the Sea of Reeds after the exodus from Egypt.—Etz Yosef
Adonoy is upon [the] many waters. The voice of Adonoy is in power,
the voice of Adonoy is in beauty.<sup class="footnote-marker">36</sup>
This translation follows S.R. Hirsch. Others translate ‘Adonoy’s voice is with power, Adonoy’s voice is with beauty.’
The voice of Adonoy breaks cedars,
Adonoy shatters the cedars of Lebanon.<sup class="footnote-marker">37</sup>
The Psalmist refers to a forest in the Holy Land where there is an abundance of tall cedar trees.—Radak
He makes them leap like a calf,
Lebanon and Sirion like unicorns. The voice of Adonoy hews out flames of fire.<sup class="footnote-marker">38</sup>

When God spoke at Sinai, His commandments came forth like a flame in the form of visible letters and words. These letters penetrated the tablets of stone and engraved themselves on them.—Rashi According to Radak the verse describes how God’s wrath will pour down upon His enemies like a bolt of fiery lightning.
The voice of Adonoy makes the desert tremble,
Adonoy makes tremble the desert of Kadesh. The voice of Adonoy causes hinds to calve,

The birth canal of the hind is very narrow and it is often impossible for the offspring to pass through. God’s voice in the thunder frightens the hind and causes it to have such strong contractions that the canal expands and the offspring is born.—Rashi
and in His Sanctuary all proclaim [His] glory. Adonoy sat enthroned (even) at the flood<sup class="footnote-marker">40</sup>
Even in the face of the total corruption of mankind at the time of the flood, God sat unchanged and unshaken upon the throne of His Sovereignty.—S.R. Hirsch
Adonoy is enthroned as King forever. Adonoy will give strength to His people;
Adonoy will bless His people with peace.<sup class="footnote-marker">41</sup>
After the coming of the Messiah there will be an end to all wars and conflicts.—Radak
This prayer was composed by Rabbi Nechunya ben Hakanah, a Tanna of the second century.
by the force of Your great right hand,
Those who study holy Torah which promulgates Your Unity.—Etz Yosef
preserve them like the pupil [of Your eye].
<small>This poem was written by Rabbi Solomon Halevy Alkabetz,
whose name שְׁלֹמֹה הַלֵוִי is spelled out by the first letter of each stanza. In this poem,

the bridegroom (Israel) calls to his Beloved Friend (God) asking that He join him in welcoming his bride (the Sabbath). The concept of welcoming the Sabbath goes back to Talmudic times. Rabbi Chanina robed himself and stood at sunset on the eve of the Sabbath and exclaimed,
“Come! Let us go forth to welcome the Sabbath Queen.” Rabbi Yanai garbed himself in festive attire on Sabbath eve and exclaimed;
<i class="footnote">“Preserve” and “Remember” refers to the discrepancy between the two texts of the fourth commandment. Exodus (20:8) reads,
“Preserve the Sabbath day.” The Talmud (Shavuos 20b) explains that both words,
שָׁמוֹר and זָכוֹר were miraculously pronounced by God simultaneously.
in a single utterance the One Almighty caused us to hear;

These words revert back to the first lines of this stanza: “The One Almighty God caused us to hear for our fame, for our glory, and for our praise.” This thought is based on the verse in Deuteronomy 28:18,19, “Keep the commandments, and He will make you high above all nations—in praise, in name, and in glory.”—Iyun Tefilah
come let us go for it is the source of blessing;

This sentence is based on the Midrashic illustration of the architect who prepares the plans for the entire structure before beginning the construction. Analogously, the Sabbath is the end-purpose of God’s creation, for which everything else was made.
dress up in your garments of glory,
through the son of Yishai the Bethlehemite,
The Messiah is a descendant of David, the son of Yishai of Bethlehem.
draw near to my soul and redeem it.
Feel not ashamed or humiliated why are you bowed down,
why do you moan? In you will take refuge the poor of my people;
Others translate “The afflicted of my people will take refuge in you.”
and the city will be rebuilt on its ancient site.
Right and left you will spread out. and Adonoy,
This translation follows Iyun Tefilah. Others translate, “will you revere.”
through the man descended from Peretz<sup class="footnote-marker">50</sup>
Peretz was the son of Judah from whom David was descended.
<small>The chazzan and congregation turn to face the entrance while reciting this verse. While saying the words בּוֹאִי כַלָּה ,
bow and turn back, to signify that the Sabbath is entering.
The husband is Israel; and the Sabbath is Israel’s crowning glory.
amidst the faithful of the treasured people. Come Bride,
a song for the Shabbos day. It is good to thank<sup class="footnote-marker">52</sup>

The Sabbath, more than other days, lends itself to offering praise and thanksgiving to God. When man rests from his physical labor and is relieved of material concerns, his soul is free to pursue the intellectual and spiritual aspects of life. These pursuits lead him to serve God and to praise Him.—Radak
and sing praise to Your Name,
Most High. To relate Your kindliness in the morning,
and Your faithfulness in the nights.<sup class="footnote-marker">53</sup>
We will proclaim His kindliness in the morning of redemption. And while yet in the darkness of exile we proclaim our belief in His faithfulness.—Rashi
Upon a ten-stringed instrument and lute,
in meditation upon the harp. For You have given me joy,
at the work of Your hands<sup class="footnote-marker">54</sup>
The Sabbath day of rest affords me the opportunity to observe and appreciate the greatness of Your work.—Radak
I sing joyously. How great are Your works,
how infinitely profound are Your thoughts.<sup class="footnote-marker">55</sup>
God’s ‘works’ are the visible creation, while His ‘thoughts’ are the Divine purpose behind each created thing.—Seporno
nor does a fool understand this: When the wicked bloom like grass,
and all the evildoers blossom— it is so that they may be destroyed forever. But You will remain on high forever Adonoy. For behold,
dispersed shall be all evildoers. You uplifted my horn<sup class="footnote-marker">56</sup>
Others translate, ‘You have increased my might like that of the wild ram.’
I am saturated with fresh oil. My eye has seen [the defeat of] those who spy on me;
of the wicked who rise against me,
my ears have heard [that they are doomed]. The righteous will blossom like a date palm,
The palm and the cedar both enjoy a long life span and flourish during all seasons. Thus they symbolize the lasting happiness of the righteous in contrast to the short prosperity of the wicked.
he will grow tall. Planted in the House of Adonoy,
in the courtyards of our God they will blossom. They will still be fruitful in old age;
they will be full of sap and freshness. To declare that Adonoy is upright;
in Whom there is no injustice.
Adonoy had begun His reign He has clothed Himself with majesty;
On the sixth day, the Levites sang Psalm 93, ‘Adonoy is King, He has clothed Himself in majesty,’ because He completed the work of creating and reigned over all His creatures.—Rosh Hashana 31a
He has girded Himself with strength. He has firmly established the world so that it cannot be moved. Your throne stands firm from of old,
You are from eternity. The rivers have raised—Adonoy— the rivers have raised their voice,
the rivers raise their raging waves. More than the sound of many waters,
mightier than the breakers of the sea Mighty on high,
Adonoy. Your testimonies are extremely faithful,
holiness is becoming to Your House,

Exalted and sanctified be His great Name in the world which He created according to His will and may He rule His kingdom bring forth His redemption and hasten the coming of His Mashiach in your lifetime and in your days,
and in the lifetime of the entire House of Israel,
speedily and in the near future— and say Amein. May His great Name be blessed forever and for all eternity. Blessed and praised,
honored and elevated and extolled be the Name of the Holy One,
far above) all the blessings and hymns,
praises and consolations which we utter in the world—and say Amein.
May there be abundant peace from heaven and good life for us and for all Israel,
—and say Amein. He Who makes peace (
the peace) in His high heavens may He,
make peace for us and or all Israel,

issues.detail: English segment e1 contains extra text ('And it is written...') not present in Hebrew h41.
